claude.country: Multi-country (English, Chinese, Malay, Thai, Persian settings)

links.outcome: Model performance across patient languages in clinical tasks
links.effect: Performance degraded from high- to low-resource languages: HealthBench 0.3743 to 0.3180; glaucoma accuracy 50.7% to 32.7%; ICU parameter recall 100.0% to 48.5%.
links.quote: LLMs/VLMs performance degraded consistently from high-to low-resource languages across al l tasks.

links.outcome: AI performance on non-English inputs, including low-resource languages
links.effect: Radiology macro-F1 fell from 0.2938 to 0.2149-0.2424, consistent with selective pathology suppression; Thai-pivot correction burden 59.0% vs English-pivot 50.7% (p=0.003).
links.quote: Multilingual deployment produced clinically consequential failures, including missed pathology, distorted physiological extraction, and amplified multimodal misclassification, that were invisible to monolingual validation and not reliably flagged by model confidence.

links.outcome: Performance gaps across language subgroups masked by monolingual validation
links.effect: Failures across languages were invisible to monolingual validation; performance degraded consistently from high- to low-resource languages across all tasks.
links.quote: Multilingual deployment produced clinically consequential failures, including missed pathology, distorted physiological extraction, and amplified multimodal misclassification, that were invisible to monolingual validation and not reliably flagged by model confidence.

links.outcome: Ability of model confidence (perplexity) to flag erroneous outputs
links.effect: Perplexity-based confidence failed to flag errors (AUROC 0.41-0.66).
links.quote: perplexity-based confidence failed to flag errors (AUROC 0·41–0·66).

links.outcome: Proportion of AI-generated records needing physician edits in prospective study
links.effect: 98.7% of records required physician edits; overall modification score 53.6%.
links.quote: In the prospective study, 98·7% of records required physician edits (overall modification score 53·6%); Thai-pivot correction burden (59·0%) exceeded English-pivot (5 0·7%, p=0·003) and Chinese-direct (51·0%, p=0·004).

unlisted_practices: Back-translation pivot inference to restore performance in low-resource languages
Token-level uncertainty toolkit to localise reasoning instability

screen.reason: Evaluates multilingual safety degradations across clinical tasks, tests deployment inference paradigms (back-translation pivot vs native language) and an uncertainty audit toolkit to detect unsafe outputs, including physician review.
